caveats: Predicted coordinates, not experimental; every number inherits the predictor's error, and contact tests are sensitive to side-chain placement.
The fractions are only as good as the flags: a mis-assigned hotspot produces a confident number measuring the wrong thing (G7 Limits).

The 10.0 A shell cutoff is a free parameter with no calibration behind it. On a 9-residue discriminating surface the shell reaches well into the invariant helices, which makes a LOW off-epitope fraction easier to achieve than it reads.
Nothing here says a contact is favourable; it says only where contact fell.
